AuroraStay Hotels | AS-01 | Internal operating policy Page 2 1. Scope and governing rules This policy applies to individual transient reservations made through an AuroraStay website, call center, property, authorized travel advisor, or approved online travel agency. The reservation confirmation controls when it contains a rate rule that is more specific than this baseline. Group, negotiated corporate, government, wholesale, crew, and extended-stay agreements may have separate written terms. The reservation record must show the property, arrival and departure dates, room type, number of guests, rate plan, payment method, cancellation deadline, taxes and disclosed fees. Staff must read the exact rate plan before promising a cancellation, change, refund, upgrade, or fee waiver. Guest-facing summary Flexible rates can normally be canceled by 6:00 PM local property time one day before arrival without a room charge. Advance Purchase rates are generally non-refundable and cannot be changed. The confirmation controls if it states a different rule. 2. Rate plan rules Rate plan Payment Cancel or change Staff action Flexible Card guarantee; payment at hotel unless confirmation says otherwise Cancel by 6:00 PM local property time one day before arrival. Later cancellation or no-show

plan rules Rate plan Payment Cancel or change Staff action Flexible Card guarantee; payment at hotel unless confirmation says otherwise Cancel by 6:00 PM local property time one day before arrival. Later cancellation or no-show is one night plus applicable tax. Quote the deadline in local property time and note the confirmation number. Advance Purchase Full stay charged at booking Non-refundable and non-changeable except where the confirmation, law, or an approved service recovery permits an exception. Do not promise a refund. Escalate documented extraordinary circumstances to a manager. Member or promotional Varies by offer Use the offer terms shown at booking. A member discount does not by itself make a rate flexible. Read the cancellation line, not only the promotional name. Group or negotiated Per signed agreement Use the signed contract or group block terms. The baseline rule does not override a contract. Send contract questions to Sales or the assigned account owner. For reservations made through an online travel agency, the agency may process the charge and cancellation. AuroraStay should confirm the agency's terms and avoid promising that the hotel can reverse an agency charge directly.

AuroraStay Hotels | AS-01 | Internal operating policy Page 3 3. Changes, no-shows, and special circumstances A guest may request a date, room type, occupancy, or property change. Staff must price the modified reservation using the current available rate and verify whether the original rate plan permits the change. A modification is not complete until the new confirmation is issued. If a guest does not arrive by the property cutoff, the reservation is treated as a no-show unless the guest has arranged a late arrival. The baseline charge is one night plus applicable tax for flexible rates. A multi-night reservation may be released after the first night unless the property has received payment or written notice for the rest of the stay. If a property cannot honor a confirmed reservation because of an overbooking or an operational closure, the manager on duty must arrange a comparable room when feasible, cover approved reasonable relocation costs, and document the resolution. The manager must not describe a relocation as a guest cancellation. A manager may approve a one-time exception for a documented service failure, duplicate booking, verified system error, or other approved service

document the resolution. The manager must not describe a relocation as a guest cancellation. A manager may approve a one-time exception for a documented service failure, duplicate booking, verified system error, or other approved service recovery. The reason, approver, amount, and guest communication must be recorded in the reservation record. 4. Taxes, deposits, and guarantees Item Baseline rule What to tell the guest Room and occupancy tax Applied according to the property location and current tax setup. Show the estimated total and explain that the final amount can change if local taxes or disclosed fees change. Incidentals authorization A temporary card authorization may be placed at arrival. The amount is property-specific and may be increased if charges are posted. It is a hold, not a final charge. Release timing depends on the issuer after checkout. Card guarantee The card must be valid and authorized under the reservation terms. A failed guarantee requires prompt guest contact or manager review. Use a valid card or an approved payment method before the cancellation deadline when required. AuroraStay does not store full payment card numbers in guest notes. Staff must use the approved payment

or manager review. Use a valid card or an approved payment method before the cancellation deadline when required. AuroraStay does not store full payment card numbers in guest notes. Staff must use the approved payment system and follow PCI DSS controls. Never request a card number by email or ordinary chat.

AuroraStay Hotels | AS-04 | Internal operating policy Page 2 1. Purpose and guest standard AuroraStay wants a safe, clean, and welcoming stay for guests, visitors, and staff. These guidelines apply in guest rooms, public areas, parking areas, meeting spaces, and property-operated transportation. They supplement the reservation terms, posted notices, emergency instructions, and applicable law. Staff should address conduct concerns early, use neutral language, and apply rules consistently. A staff member should not confront a guest alone when there is a safety risk. Contact the manager on duty or emergency services according to the severity of the situation. Immediate safety rule Call 911 for an immediate threat to life, serious injury, fire, active violence, or suspected crime in progress. Notify the manager on duty when safe. Do not delay emergency care to complete a complaint record. 2. Core conduct rules Topic Guideline Response if not followed Quiet hours Quiet hours are 10:00 PM to 7:00 AM local property time. Guests must keep noise at a level that does not unreasonably disturb others at all times. Contact the room when safe, document the complaint, and escalate repeat or serious disturbances. Smoking

AM local property time. Guests must keep noise at a level that does not unreasonably disturb others at all times. Contact the room when safe, document the complaint, and escalate repeat or serious disturbances. Smoking and vaping Smoking and vaping are prohibited in guest rooms and indoor public areas unless a property specifically designates a lawful smoking area. Ask the guest to stop. Document evidence and apply an approved remediation charge only when supported. Threats and violence Threats, assault, weapons used unlawfully, and intimidation are not permitted. Move to safety, call 911 when appropriate, notify the manager, and preserve relevant evidence. Illegal activity Illegal activity, trafficking, drug distribution, and exploitation are not permitted on property. Do not investigate personally. Follow the safety and law enforcement escalation process. Visitors and parties Visitors must follow posted occupancy, registration, age, and event rules. Parties or events that create a disturbance or exceed capacity are not permitted. Ask the host to correct the issue and involve the manager if the problem continues.

AuroraStay Hotels | AS-04 | Internal operating policy Page 3 3. Accessibility and service animals AuroraStay follows the Americans with Disabilities Act Title III requirements for places of lodging and provides reasonable modifications and accessible features as required by applicable law. Staff should focus on the requested feature or task, not on the guest's diagnosis or private medical information. Question or issue Required handling A guest requests an accessible feature Ask what feature is needed, check the room and property profile, record the request, and confirm what can be provided. Escalate if the request cannot be met. A service animal is not obvious Ask only whether the animal is required because of a disability and what work or task it has been trained to perform. A service animal is out of control or not housebroken Ask the handler to correct the issue. If it is not corrected, involve the manager. Do not charge a pet fee or make a breed-based decision. A guest asks about an emotional support animal An animal that does not meet the ADA service animal definition follows the property's pet policy unless another law or approved

fee or make a breed-based decision. A guest asks about an emotional support animal An animal that does not meet the ADA service animal definition follows the property's pet policy unless another law or approved accommodation applies. A guest reports discrimination Listen, do not argue, document the facts, involve the manager, and offer the formal complaint channel. Escalate urgent safety or access concerns immediately. Staff must not demand a service animal certificate, vest, or medical record as a condition of entry. Service animals are not subject to a pet fee. A direct threat assessment must be based on objective evidence and an individualized assessment, not on stereotypes. 4. Safety, privacy, and lost property Guests should use the room safe when available and keep keys, mobile credentials, and personal information secure. Staff verify identity before issuing a replacement key, providing room information, or releasing stored luggage. Staff must not announce a guest's room number aloud in public. Lost property is logged, secured, and returned through the approved process. Staff should not open, browse, or share personal content from a found device except as needed to identify the owner through an approved

public. Lost property is logged, secured, and returned through the approved process. Staff should not open, browse, or share personal content from a found device except as needed to identify the owner through an approved procedure. Suspected weapons, drugs, exploitation, or immediate danger are handled through safety escalation, not informal investigation.

AuroraStay Hotels | AS-04 | Internal operating policy Page 4 5. Complaint resolution Stage Staff action Target Listen and stabilize Move to a safe and private setting where possible. Confirm the immediate need and acknowledge the concern without assigning blame. Immediately Clarify facts Ask what happened, when, where, who was involved, and what outcome the guest needs. Avoid leading questions. During first contact Check policy and records Review reservation, property profile, posted rule, folio, or incident record. Protect sensitive data. Same shift Offer a remedy Give the remedy the staff member can approve, or explain the manager review and follow-up time. Same shift when possible Escalate and close Escalate safety, access, discrimination, privacy, media, legal, or unresolved compensation issues. Confirm the next step to the guest. Within one business day unless urgent Neutral documentation Record observable facts, the guest's stated concern, the policy checked, the action taken, the approver, and the follow-up owner. Avoid labels such as difficult, intoxicated, or suspicious unless the specific observable behavior is recorded and the label is necessary for safety. 6. Review notes This policy should be reviewed at least annually and after a material incident, regulatory change, property acquisition, or change to payment, access, surveillance, or guest messaging systems. AuroraStay Hotels | AS-03 | Internal operating policy Page 2 1. Purpose and refund principles This guide helps guest service staff explain refunds, releases, credits, and additional charges. The reservation rate terms control eligibility. The payment method and booking channel control how the money moves. Staff must not promise a refund before checking both. Refunds generally return to the original payment method. A different method may be used only when Finance or a manager approves it and the transaction can be documented. Cash refunds are not the default for card or agency payments. Three questions before quoting a refund What was charged? What rule makes it refundable or non-refundable? Who can release or approve the funds? If any answer is unclear, say that the request is under review and give the guest a follow-up channel. 2. Common refund scenarios Scenario Baseline outcome Required verification Flexible reservation canceled on time No room charge. If a prepayment was taken, refund the eligible amount after verifying the cancellation timestamp. Rate plan, local property deadline, booking channel, and payment status. Flexible reservation canceled late or no-show One night plus applicable tax may be retained

was taken, refund the eligible amount after verifying the cancellation timestamp. Rate plan, local property deadline, booking channel, and payment status. Flexible reservation canceled late or no-show One night plus applicable tax may be retained under the baseline rule. Exact cancellation time, guest notice, property time zone, and any approved exception. Advance Purchase cancellation Normally non-refundable. Escalate only with a documented contract, system error, legal requirement, or approved service recovery. Confirmation terms, payment capture, manager approval, and reason for exception. Duplicate or incorrect charge Correct the duplicate or error and refund the excess after reconciling the folio. Folio, payment ledger, authorization, and whether the booking channel also charged. Service recovery Manager may approve a partial refund, credit, or other remedy based on the documented impact. Complaint facts, remedy offered, approver, amount, and guest acceptance.

Additional charges Charges must be disclosed in the rate, confirmation, property profile, posted notice, or guest agreement before they are applied, except for documented damage or loss assessed under the guest's agreement and applicable law. Staff must provide an itemized folio or receipt on request. Quote type, nightly amount, tax, and whether in-and-out access is included. Pet fee Property-specific per stay or per night A non-service animal stays under the property's pet policy. State amount, limit, room restriction, and whether tax applies. Do not charge service animals a pet fee. Late checkout Property-specific; may be a flat fee or additional night Guest receives an approved departure extension. Confirm the new departure time and exact fee before approval. Smoking or vaping remediation Up to $250 baseline, subject to evidence and local law Credible evidence shows smoking or vaping in a prohibited guest room or indoor area. Explain the rule, evidence category, charge basis, and dispute channel.

remediation Up to $250 baseline, subject to evidence and local law Credible evidence shows smoking or vaping in a prohibited guest room or indoor area. Explain the rule, evidence category, charge basis, and dispute channel. Do not charge based on odor alone when facts are unclear. Lost key or device Reasonable replacement cost when stated in the property terms A guest does not return a physical key, parking device, or other property asset. State the item, replacement basis, and how the guest can return it or dispute the charge. Damage or missing item Documented reasonable repair or replacement cost Inspection supports damage beyond ordinary wear or an item is missing after checkout. Provide an itemized explanation and dispute path. Do not disclose another guest's information. The $250 smoking or vaping amount is an internal baseline only. A property may publish a different amount if the guest agreement and applicable law support it. Do not invent a fee that is not in an approved source. 4. Incidentals authorization and release At arrival, the property may authorize an amount for anticipated incidentals. The authorization can reduce available credit without being a posted

a fee that is not in an approved source. 4. Incidentals authorization and release At arrival, the property may authorize an amount for anticipated incidentals. The authorization can reduce available credit without being a posted charge. When the folio is settled, the property sends a release for the unused amount. The card issuer controls how quickly the pending hold disappears; AuroraStay cannot guarantee a same-day release. If a guest sees a pending hold after checkout, staff should confirm the final folio, explain that the unused portion was released or is scheduled for release, and advise the guest to contact the card issuer if the pending status persists beyond the issuer's normal timeframe. A pending authorization is not evidence of a second final charge.

AuroraStay Hotels | AS-02 | Internal operating policy Page 3 3. Guest amenities and services Amenity hours and availability can change for maintenance, staffing, weather, or safety. The live property profile and posted notices control. Staff should answer with the current hours and location when available, not with a group-wide assumption. Hours, adult and child pricing, included rate plans, allergy handling, and holiday service. Wi-Fi Basic guest Wi-Fi is normally provided at no separate charge. Network name, premium speed, device limit, captive portal, and outage handling. Fitness and pool Available only where listed in the property profile. Hours, age rules, reservations, closures, lifeguard status, and temporary restrictions. Luggage storage May be offered by the front desk or bell team when secure capacity exists. Parking, pets, and service animals Parking is not guaranteed unless the reservation or property profile says it is reserved. Staff must quote the current parking type and charge, explain whether in-and-out access is allowed, and tell the guest how to validate or pay. Parking charges are separate from the room rate unless the confirmation says they are included. Pet rules are property-specific. A pet fee, weight limit, number limit, room restriction, and vaccination or control requirement may apply. Service animals are not pets under the ADA and are not subject to a pet fee. Staff may ask only the two ADA-permitted questions when the disability-related need is not obvious: whether the animal is required because of a disability and what work or task it has been trained to perform. An emotional support, comfort, or therapy animal that does not meet the ADA service animal definition is handled under the property's pet rule unless another

what work or task it has been trained to perform. An emotional support, comfort, or therapy animal that does not meet the ADA service animal definition is handled under the property's pet rule unless another law or approved accommodation applies. Do not request a certificate, vest, or medical record as a condition of recognizing a service animal.

AuroraStay Hotels | AS-02 | Internal operating policy Page 5 6. Accessibility and guest requests AuroraStay provides reasonable modifications and accessible features as required by applicable law. A guest may request an accessible route, mobility feature, visual or audible alert, communication support, or another accommodation. Staff should ask what feature is needed, record the request in the approved system, and confirm what the property can provide. Do not treat a request for an accessible room as an optional preference when the guest is asking for an accessibility feature. Do not disclose the guest's disability details to staff who do not need them. If the request cannot be met as stated, involve the manager on duty and offer a specific alternative without making a promise the property cannot deliver. Service animals may accompany a guest in areas open to guests, subject to the ADA rules for control, housebreaking, and direct threat.
